subject: Clarify ownership of tracking tags & telemetry consent for console flows
messages:
From: J. Patel <jpatel@acme-marketing.com>

Cc: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Tracking pixels + console telemetry — who is responsible?

Hi Olga,

We're doing a privacy review ahead of our integration pilot and had a few quick questions about the telemetry and marketing pixels that appear in the Redwood Console / hosted UI. Specifically: 

- Do any Redwood-hosted web pages served to our users set marketing cookies or fire third-party trackers (e.g., Google Analytics, Segment) on behalf of customers?
- If telemetry is captured from the Console (usage events, feature flags, crash logs), does Redwood ever forward that to downstream vendors under our account context?
- For consent — are customers expected to surface their own banner/consent widget in front of the Console, or is there an option to disable marketing/analytics telemetry at the account level?

We need these clarifications to complete our DPA addendum and to decide whether to require an explicit consent flow for our end users. I can share our internal questionnaire if that helps.

Thanks,
Jai Patel
Privacy & Data Governance
Acme Marketing

---
Attachment: acme-privacy-questions-telemetry.xlsx (spreadsheet of questions)

From: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>

Cc: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 12:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tracking pixels + console telemetry — who is responsible?

Hi Jai — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Marcus (Product) and Neha (Customer Success) so we can answer thoroughly. Quick answers up front:

- Redwood Console does not inject third-party marketing pixels on behalf of customers by default. We collect product telemetry (usage metrics, page views, feature usage) to run the service and improve reliability.
- Telemetry that is tied to an account is retained per the DPA and only exported to subprocessors listed in our subprocessor registry; we do not forward customer telemetry to marketing vendors as a default behavior.
- There is an account-level toggle to disable non-essential analytics for Dedicated/Private customers; for Hosted accounts we can apply a policy to suppress marketing telemetry if requested in the DPA addendum.

That said, there are a few ambiguous areas I want to confirm with Product: which Console assets load third-party libraries (e.g., our docs site, hosted help widget) and whether any embed we run on a customer-facing page could create cookies in the customer's domain. Marcus, can you confirm which front-end assets are customer-facing and what third-party scripts they call?

Next steps:
1) Marcus to confirm a short list of Console pages and third-party dependencies.
2) Security to produce a subprocessor export filtered for Acme's account and evidence (SCC/DPA clauses) that we apply.
3) Draft a recommended consent blurb for Acme to use if they want explicit opt-in on the hosted login/embedded widgets.

Olga
VP, Accounts & Privacy Liaison
Redwood Inference

From: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, J. Patel <jpatel@acme-marketing.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 08:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tracking pixels + console telemetry — who is responsible?

Hi all — quick technical breakdown from Product side: 

1) Customer-facing embeds: our "Deploy" snippet (JS snippet customers copy into their app to embed a chat widget) will call our CDN-hosted assets. That snippet will set a first-party cookie on the customer's site (domain-bound) for session continuity; it does not add third-party marketing pixels.

2) Console & Docs: the Console itself loads Google Analytics only for product telemetry; GA is configured on our redwood.ai domain and we do not configure GA to read or write cookies on customer domains. Docs are on a separate docs.redwood.ai host and may have a small number of analytics scripts (GA + Sentry). We can provide a stripped docs build without analytics for customers who require it.

3) Downstream exports: by default we do not export account telemetry to marketing vendors. However, customers can enable integrations (e.g., Segment) from the Console which will cause event exports to that integration destination. This is an opt-in toggle per account.

4) Consent controls: for Hosted accounts we surface "Data sharing integrations" in Settings with an allowlist toggle. For Dedicated/Private, we can turn off outbound integrations at the org level. There is no universal global switch that overrides embedded scripts on customer domains — the snippet behavior is intentionally first-party.

Recommendation: provide Acme with (a) a subprocessor list filtered to only the vendors that touch telemetry for their account, (b) docs on how to disable analytics on our docs/console, and (c) a recommended consent snippet for their UI if they plan to gather marketing consent from end users.

Marcus
Head of Product, Console
Redwood Inference
